heuristics.name: antonym-pair
heuristics.description: When two options are clear opposites, assume the distractor brief paired the key with its antonym; pick one pole (usually the more 'headword-gloss-like' one).

heuristics.name: odd-valence
heuristics.description: Pick the option whose sentiment or category differs from the other three.

heuristics.name: mixed-part-of-speech
heuristics.description: When options mix parts of speech, pick the one consistent with a plausible two-sense headword.

heuristics.name: none
heuristics.description: No usable signal; pick made arbitrarily (often by imagining which option is a standard gloss of a common ISEE headword, which does not discriminate since every option is such a gloss).

notes: Every option reads as a plain gloss of some plausible ISEE headword, so options rarely discriminate. Antonym pairs were the only recurrent structural cue and are weak: the key could equally be either pole or neither. No reject can be certain without the headword.
